svg.text: One deployment per hospital (AWS CDK, EU region). Layer 1 is the validated platform, deployed once; Layer 2 is the apps: manifests — data, not code — produced by a compiler and run by a deterministic renderer.
single-page app in the browser, served by CloudFront
identity masking per role · OHIF viewer
AWS account of the hospital — Layer 1, deployed once with CDK
sign-in for every panel user · platform groups: authors, approvers, viewers, admins
per-app role groups created at publish · federation to the hospital IdP (stretch)
JWT authorizer on the ID token
re-validates manifest and role · applies the
scope server-side · audit record per call
Strands Agents on Bedrock · fills the
AppSpec through tools, never writes code
expires 30 days after the last change
read and write through the dispatcher
QIDO-RS study lists via the dispatcher
WADO-RS images to the OHIF viewer
Compiler and renderer are one verified codebase: a manifest only ever contains catalog components and data primitives; anything else is refused before it reaches a clinician.
Every data call — read or write — goes through the dispatcher, which recomputes the role's scope from the stored manifest; the browser is never trusted.
clinical use — open an app; every data call through the dispatcher
authoring — chat → AppSpec → compiler → registry → sign-off → publish
